startup.name: Volaren
startup.one_liner: The personal investing agent that comes to you
startup.description: Four person San Francisco consumer fintech. Users connect bank and brokerage accounts; an AI agent explains why the portfolio moved, answers money questions, suggests ideas and places trades. It supports copying famous investors, politicians, strategies and themed baskets, and user built agents that act within set limits, through an app, the web or text messages.

yc_acceptance.basis: Test mode: assumed accepted to YC for Fall 2026. The prior is about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band, and no adjustment is made because acceptance is not forecast in this test.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not scored in this blind test because the company was accepted, so the number shown is only the unadjusted prior. YC would most plausibly have passed because Robinhood, Public and others already ship AI agents for investing, and trading copy features raise regulatory and loss liability issues for a four person team.

ladder.why_it_fails: Investors in October 2026 already see Robinhood agentic trading and Public's agents, and ask why a four person team wins consumer distribution. The agent needs brokerage rails through a partner, and a copy trading feature is a regulatory question. Finary raised a $3.2M seed on community distribution but later shut down, and TAI, a three person investing app, only raised about $0.5M. Without a clear acquisition channel, seed slips.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A needs funded accounts, revenue per user above acquisition cost and a clear regulatory path. Retail trading apps have thin revenue per user unless they hold payment for order flow or subscriptions, and giants subsidize the same features free. Finary, Botin and TAI show that investing apps with no strong channel stall. A pivot to infrastructure like SnapTrade is the path that sometimes works.

ladder.why_it_fails: Reaching a C would need a license, large assets and a defensible product against Robinhood and Public. More likely endings are acquisition by a broker or wealth platform. Few retail investing apps among the analogs reached a C.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likeliest end is a stall or a soft acquisition as incumbents ship agents and consumer investing apps have weak revenue per user. Regulation and loss liability add risk. A larger result needs becoming the default agent for a large user base, which the big brokers are also chasing.

killers.risk: Incumbent brokers ship the same agent free
killers.evidence: Robinhood launched agentic trading and Public launched agents in 2026, with large user bases.
killers.mitigation: Focus on an underserved niche such as copy strategies and text first, or sell the engine to brokers.

killers.risk: Regulation of advice and copy trading
killers.evidence: Recommending trades and acting for users can require adviser registration, and copying politicians or investors raises disclosure issues.
killers.mitigation: Partner with a registered broker and keep user set limits.

killers.risk: No cheap channel to acquire retail users
killers.evidence: Consumer fintech acquisition cost is high and revenue per user is low.
killers.mitigation: Use text and creator led growth.

killers.risk: Agent losses create liability and churn
killers.evidence: A live money trial of AI trading portfolios lost about a third of capital, and one broker's terms exclude agent loss compensation.
killers.mitigation: Cap risk and show clear explanations.

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage integration, portfolio explanations from models and trade execution are buildable by four people through partners. Hard parts are reliability, compliance and keeping models from giving harmful advice.

takeover_risk.rationale: Several brokers already ship agents and have the accounts and licenses. A small company depends on their data access and could be cut off.

Robinhood and Public both launched agent trading in 2026, which shows demand and a crowded field.

brand.rationale: A short invented word is common among recent YC consumer winners and is easy to say and spell in a text message. Trust matters in money apps, and a name alone does not build it, so I left the ladder unchanged.

narrative.headline: A timely idea that Robinhood and Public already ship, so odds rest on a niche and a distribution channel.
narrative.general_summary: Volaren is a four person team building a text first AI agent for personal investing, with copy trading and user built agents. Demand for AI help in investing is real, but Robinhood and Public both launched agent trading in 2026 with huge user bases. Consumer fintech cohorts show about 57 percent reaching a seed and 23 percent an A, and investing app analogs such as Finary and TAI stalled without a channel. I stay near those anchors, with a small discount to seed for the crowded field and regulatory risk, and keep later stages within 0.75x of the base rates.
